dm: and it would become a grasping at a sentient being, a grasping at a life-force, and a grasping at a person.
gm: grasp at a sentient being, grasp at a living soul, and grasp at a person.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, a bodhisattva should not grasp at phenomena as being erroneous, nor should they grasp at what is not a phenomenon.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, it is because a bodhisattva should not wrongly grasp at a dharma, nor should they grasp at a non-dharma.

dm: Therefore, keeping this in mind, the Tathāgata has said that those who understand this discourse on the Dharma as being like a raft should abandon even phenomena, let alone what are not phenomena.
gm: Therefore, with this in mind, the Tathāgata has spoken: 'Those who know this dharma discourse to be like a raft should abandon even dharmas, let alone non-dharmas.'

dm: Furthermore, the Blessed One spoke these words to the venerable Subhūti:
gm: Furthermore, the Blessed One spoke thus to the Venerable Subhūti:

dm: Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: Subhūti, what do you think of this?

dm: Do you think that there is any phenomenon whatsoever by which the Tathāgata has fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
gm: Do you think there is any dharma whatsoever to which the Tathāgata has manifestly and completely awakened as unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening?

dm: Do you think that there is any phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has taught?
gm: Do you think there is any dharma whatsoever that has been taught by the Tathāgata?

dm: When he had spoken those words, the venerable Subhūti addressed the Blessed One in this way:
gm: When he had spoken thus, the Venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:

dm: Blessed One, as I understand the meaning of what the Blessed One has said, there is no phenomenon whatsoever by which the Tathāgata has fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
gm: Blessed One, as I understand the meaning of what the Blessed One has spoken, there is no dharma whatsoever to which the Tathāgata has manifestly and completely awakened as unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening.

dm: There is no phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has taught.
gm: There is no dharma whatsoever that has been taught by the Tathāgata.

dm: Why is that? Because the phenomena that the Tathāgata has fully awakened to, or that he has taught, are not to be grasped and are not to be expressed.
gm: Why is that? Any dharma whatsoever to which the Tathāgata has manifestly and completely awakened, or that he has taught, cannot be grasped and cannot be expressed;

dm: That is because it is neither a phenomenon nor the absence of a phenomenon.
gm: because it is neither a dharma nor a non-dharma.

dm: Why is that? Because noble individuals are distinguished by the unconditioned.
gm: Why is that? Because noble beings are distinguished by the unconditioned.

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: The Blessed One spoke: Subhūti, what do you think of this?

dm: If some son or daughter of noble family were to fill this trichiliocosm world system with the seven kinds of precious substances and give them as a gift, would that son or daughter of noble family generate much merit on that basis?
gm: If some son of noble family or daughter of noble family were to fill this three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system with the seven precious substances and give it as a gift, do you think that son of noble family or daughter of noble family would generate a great mass of merit from that basis?

dm: Subhūti replied, "Blessed One, it would be much."
gm: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, it is much.

dm: "It would be much, Sugata."
gm: Sugata, it is much.

dm: That son or daughter of noble family would generate a great mass of merit on that basis.
gm: That son of noble family or daughter of noble family would generate a great mass of merit from that basis.

dm: Why is that? Because that mass of merit is not a mass.
gm: Why is that? Because that very mass of merit is not a mass;

dm: Therefore, the Tathāgata speaks of a "mass of merit, a mass of merit."
gm: therefore the Tathāgata spoke of 'a mass of merit, a mass of merit'.

dm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, if a son or daughter of noble family were to fill this trichiliocosm of great thousand-fold world systems with the seven types of precious substances and give them as a gift, and if another were to take up from this discourse on Dharma even just a four-line verse and explain it to others and correctly demonstrate it, they would generate a mass of merit from that basis that is far greater, incalculable, and immeasurable.
gm: The Blessed One spoke: Subhūti, compared to some son of noble family or daughter of noble family filling this three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system with the seven precious substances and giving it as a gift, whoever takes up even just a four-line verse from this discourse on dharma, teaches it to others, and perfectly explains it will generate a much greater mass of merit from that basis, countless and immeasurable.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and perfectly complete Buddhas arises from this.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, the unexcelled, perfectly complete awakening of the Tathāgatas, the Arhats, the perfectly complete Buddhas arises from this;

dm: Because the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are also born from this.
gm: because the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are also born from this.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, what are called "Buddha-qualities, Buddha-qualities" are spoken of by the Tathāgata as being devoid of those Buddha-qualities.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, as for what are called 'the dharmas of a Buddha, the dharmas of a Buddha', because the Tathāgata spoke of those dharmas of a Buddha as non-existent;

dm: Therefore, they are called "Buddha-qualities."
gm: therefore they are called 'the dharmas of a Buddha'.
